    <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","headline":"calico-typha hangs during unclean client TLS handshake","articleBody":"\u003c!--- Provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above --\u003e\r\nOn certain special conditions, a client TLS handshake can block the typha server indefinitely, as you can see [here](https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/60f8a9e884567ca690487849ff9df991091eced0/typha/pkg/syncserver/sync_server.go#L427), the `Handshake()` call is performed inside the main server handle `for` loop, without any timeout, so a miss behaving client, with an unclean TLS handshake, can take the server down and block the main loop indefinitely while other connections will be setting idle and waiting for that handshake to eventually finish.\r\n\r\n## Expected Behavior\r\n\u003c!--- If you're describing a bug, tell us what should happen --\u003e\r\n\u003c!--- If you're suggesting a change/improvement, tell us how it should work --\u003e\r\nA misbehaving client should not impact the availability of the typha server, the TLS handshake must be performed with a safe upper timeout and eventually moved out of the main server handle `for` loop.\r\n\r\n## Current Behavior\r\n\u003c!--- If describing a bug, tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior --\u003e\r\n\u003c!--- If suggesting a change/improvement, explain the difference from current behavior --\u003e\r\nThe client TLS handshake is performed in the main server handle `for` loop without a safe timeout, misbehaving clients can impact the availability of the typha server if the connection is not clearly closed/aborted at client side.\r\n\r\n## Possible Solution\r\n\u003c!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug, --\u003e\r\n\u003c!--- or ideas how to implement the addition or change --\u003e\r\n\r\n1. Implement a timeout in the TLS handshake to the duration of one Ping interval.\r\n2. Eventually move the TLS handshake to an async go routine and unblock the main server handle `for` loop, so multiple client connections could be handled at the same time.\r\n\r\n## Steps to Reproduce (for bugs)\r\n\u003c!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to --\u003e\r\n\u003c!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant --\u003e\r\n1. Perform a few cycles of Kubernetes cluster growth and shrink, eventually one of the nodes running the `calico-node` client will be abruptly terminated during client TLS handshake, leaving the connection towards the `calico-typha` hanging in an unclean state during TLS handshake, the `calico-typha` will never, under a reasonable time, recover from that, the server will be blocked for days and eventually all `calico-typha` replicas will get to the same state, bringing the node network down.\r\n2. Another easy way to simulate this is to perform a `port-forward` to a `calico-typha` pod at port `5473` and then open a `telnet` connection to that port, the typha server will hang with a message like the following and other clients won't be able to connect to that typha server anymore:\r\n```\r\n2023-08-07 15:12:57.284 [INFO][7] sync_server.go 421: Accepted from xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:60824 port=5473\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Context\r\n\u003c!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? --\u003e\r\n\u003c!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world --\u003e\r\nThis issue can eventually bring a Kubernetes production cluster running Calico with calico-typha completely down, please keep in mind the error is only reproduced on certain special conditions, during race conditions in the client termination in the exact moment of a TLS handshake with the typha server, over time, that can affect all replicas of the typha deployment, bringing the availability of the cluster network down.\r\n\r\n## Your Environment\r\n\u003c!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in --\u003e\r\n* Calico version - `v3.26.1`\r\n* Orchestrator version (e.g. kubernetes, mesos, rkt): `kubernetes` using the `tigera-operator`\r\n* Operating System and version: AWS EKS using Amazon EKS optimized Amazon Linux AMIs\r\n* Link to your project (optional):\r\n","author":{"url":"https://github.com/rodrigorfk","@type":"Person","name":"rodrigorfk"},"datePublished":"2023-08-08T10:25:40.000Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"https://schema.org/CommentAction","userInteractionCount":2},"url":"https://github.com/7908/calico/issues/7908"}</script>

<p dir="auto">On certain special conditions, a client TLS handshake can block the typha server indefinitely, as you can see <a href="https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/60f8a9e884567ca690487849ff9df991091eced0/typha/pkg/syncserver/sync_server.go#L427">here</a>, the <code class="notranslate">Handshake()</code> call is performed inside the main server handle <code class="notranslate">for</code> loop, without any timeout, so a miss behaving client, with an unclean TLS handshake, can take the server down and block the main loop indefinitely while other connections will be setting idle and waiting for that handshake to eventually finish.</p>
<h2 dir="auto">Expected Behavior</h2>


<p dir="auto">A misbehaving client should not impact the availability of the typha server, the TLS handshake must be performed with a safe upper timeout and eventually moved out of the main server handle <code class="notranslate">for</code> loop.</p>
<h2 dir="auto">Current Behavior</h2>


<p dir="auto">The client TLS handshake is performed in the main server handle <code class="notranslate">for</code> loop without a safe timeout, misbehaving clients can impact the availability of the typha server if the connection is not clearly closed/aborted at client side.</p>
<h2 dir="auto">Possible Solution</h2>


<ol dir="auto">
<li>Implement a timeout in the TLS handshake to the duration of one Ping interval.</li>
<li>Eventually move the TLS handshake to an async go routine and unblock the main server handle <code class="notranslate">for</code> loop, so multiple client connections could be handled at the same time.</li>
</ol>
<h2 dir="auto">Steps to Reproduce (for bugs)</h2>


<ol dir="auto">
<li>Perform a few cycles of Kubernetes cluster growth and shrink, eventually one of the nodes running the <code class="notranslate">calico-node</code> client will be abruptly terminated during client TLS handshake, leaving the connection towards the <code class="notranslate">calico-typha</code> hanging in an unclean state during TLS handshake, the <code class="notranslate">calico-typha</code> will never, under a reasonable time, recover from that, the server will be blocked for days and eventually all <code class="notranslate">calico-typha</code> replicas will get to the same state, bringing the node network down.</li>
<li>Another easy way to simulate this is to perform a <code class="notranslate">port-forward</code> to a <code class="notranslate">calico-typha</code> pod at port <code class="notranslate">5473</code> and then open a <code class="notranslate">telnet</code> connection to that port, the typha server will hang with a message like the following and other clients won't be able to connect to that typha server anymore:</li>
</ol>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="2023-08-07 15:12:57.284 [INFO][7] sync_server.go 421: Accepted from xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:60824 port=5473"><pre class="notranslate"><code class="notranslate">2023-08-07 15:12:57.284 [INFO][7] sync_server.go 421: Accepted from xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:60824 port=5473
</code></pre></div>
<h2 dir="auto">Context</h2>


<p dir="auto">This issue can eventually bring a Kubernetes production cluster running Calico with calico-typha completely down, please keep in mind the error is only reproduced on certain special conditions, during race conditions in the client termination in the exact moment of a TLS handshake with the typha server, over time, that can affect all replicas of the typha deployment, bringing the availability of the cluster network down.</p>
<h2 dir="auto">Your Environment</h2>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>Calico version - <code class="notranslate">v3.26.1</code></li>
<li>Orchestrator version (e.g. kubernetes, mesos, rkt): <code class="notranslate">kubernetes</code> using the <code class="notranslate">tigera-operator</code></li>
<li>Operating System and version: AWS EKS using Amazon EKS optimized Amazon Linux AMIs</li>
